p: teacheth my hands to war: Who out of a poor shepherd has made a valiant warrior and mighty conqueror.
subdueth my people under me: He confesses that neither by his own authority, power or policy was his kingdom quiet, but by the secret grace of God.
takest knowledge of him: To give to God just praise, is to confess ourselves to be unworthy of so excellent benefits, and that he bestows them on us of his free mercy.
Bow thy heavens: He desires God to continue his graces, and to send help for the present need.
Cast forth lightning: By these manner of speeches he shows that all the hindrances in the world cannot prevent God's power, which he apprehends by faith.
waters: That is, deliver me from the tumults of they who should be my people but are corrupt in their judgment and enterprises, as though they were strangers.
of falsehood: For though they shake hands, they do not keep their promises.
new song unto thee: That is, a rare and excellent song, as your great benefits deserve.

servant from the hurtful sword: Though wicked kings are called God's servants, as was Cyrus in Isa 45:1, for he uses them to execute his judgments: yet David because of God's promise and they who rule godly are properly so called, because they do not serve their own affections, but set forth God's glory.
That our sons may be as: He desires God to continue his benefits toward his people, counting the procreation of children and their good education among the chiefest of God's benefits.
garners may be full: That the corners of our houses may be full of store for the great abundance of your blessings.
oxen may be strong to labour: He attributes not only the great conveniences, but even the least also to God's favour.
And if God does not give to all his children all these blessings, yet he replaces them with better things.
